extracted.intended_audience: Users of the GAP computer algebra system working with semigroups and monoids (mathematicians, computational algebraists, advanced students)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for semigroup/monoid properties and operations in GAP, including predicates (Is...), constructors, and utility functions for Green's relations, Rees matrix semigroups, ideals, quotients, and finitely presented semigroups/monoids.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid / GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup / GeneratorsOfMonoid / GeneratorsOfSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Different generating sets can be produced depending on whether one wants generators that define an inverse monoid, inverse semigroup, monoid, or semigroup. Use GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid, GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup, GeneratorsOfMonoid, and GeneratorsOfSemigroup to obtain the respective generating sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documentation notes there are four different possible generating sets which define an inverse monoid; pick the GeneratorsOf* function appropriate to the algebraic structure you wish to generate. Example usage: GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid(S) returns generating set displayed for S.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInverseSubsemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsInverseSubsemigroup(S, T) returns true if the semigroup T is an inverse subsemigroup of the semigroup S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to check whether T inherits the inverse-semi-group structure within S. Examples show using InverseSemigroup(RandomPartialPerm(4)) and testing membership in SymmetricInverseSemigroup(4) or FullTransformationSemigroup(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRegularSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRegularSemigroup(S) returns true if S is regular, i.e., if every D-class of S is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularity is defined via D-classes; check IsRegularSemigroup when you need to know if every element has a (general) inverse in the semigroup structure at the D-class level.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRegularSemigroupElement
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRegularSemigroupElement(S, x) returns true if x has a general inverse in S, i.e., there exists y in S with x*y*x = x and y*x*y = y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test regularity of a single element. The manual shows calling IsRegularSemigroupElement(S, x) after computing inverses; computation may depend on the semigroup representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: InversesOfSemigroupElement
rubrics_metrics.description: InversesOfSemigroupElement(S, x) returns a list of the inverses of the element x in the semigroup S. An element y is an inverse of x iff x*y*x = x and y*x*y = y. x has an inverse iff x is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns all inverses; examples show returning lists of Transformations or ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement tuples. Use Set(...) if order/duplicates are irrelevant. Note: Inverses exist exactly when element is regular.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSimpleSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSimpleSemigroup(S) is true iff the semigroup S has no proper ideals (i.e., is simple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to detect simplicity. The manual relates simplicity of Rees matrix semigroups to underlying semigroup simplicity and shows examples under ReesMatrix isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsZeroSimpleSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsZeroSimpleSemigroup(S) is true iff the semigroup S (with zero) has no proper ideals except for 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applies to semigroups with a zero element; if GAP cannot find a zero it may enter a break-loop. A finite Rees 0-matrix semigroup is 0-simple iff every row and column of its matrix has a non-zero entry and the underlying semigroup is simple.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsZeroGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsZeroGroup(S) returns true iff the semigroup S is a group with zero adjoined (a group plus a zero element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detects group-with-zero structure; used when analyzing semigroup structures that might be group-like with an absorbing zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsReesCongruenceSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsReesCongruenceSemigroup(S) returns true if every congruence of S is a Rees congruence (i.e., congruences arise from ideals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to detect the special property that congruences are exactly Rees congruences; relates to ideal structure of the semigroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInverseSemigroup / IsInverseMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: IsInverseSemigroup(S) (and IsInverseMonoid(S)) returns true iff every element x in S has a unique semigroup inverse y with x*y*x = x and y*x*y = y. A monoid that is an inverse semigroup is called an inverse monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category predicate for inverse semigroup/monoid. Examples show testing semigroups constructed from Transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SemigroupIdealByGenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: SemigroupIdealByGenerators(S, gens) returns the two-sided ideal of semigroup S generated by the list gens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs ideals by generators; used as basis for forming Rees congruences (see ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal(I) returns the congruence on S given by Δ ∪ I × I, where I is a two-sided ideal of a semigroup S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the standard Rees congruence associated to an ideal; used when building quotient semigroups collapsing an ideal to a singleton class.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLeftSemigroupIdeal / IsRightSemigroupIdeal / IsSemigroupIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: IsLeftSemigroupIdeal(I), IsRightSemigroupIdeal(I), and IsSemigroupIdeal(I) are category/property predicates returning whether I is a left ideal, right ideal, or two-sided ideal respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these predicates to check ideal-type properties of subsets/semigroups. They are attributes/properties in GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSemigroupCongruence
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSemigroupCongruence(c) returns true if c is a congruence on the semigroup (i.e., a magma congruence on the semigroup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semigroup congruences are handled via the magma congruence machinery; use IsSemigroupCongruence to verify input before quotient operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsReesCongruence
rubrics_metrics.description: IsReesCongruence(c) returns true iff the congruence c has at most one non-singleton congruence class (i.e., is a Rees congruence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify Rees congruences specifically; typically arises from ideals via ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: QuotientSemigroup constructs and predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: IsQuotientSemigroup(S) identifies semigroups constructed as quotients; HomomorphismQuotientSemigroup(cong) returns the homomorphism from S to the quotient by cong; QuotientSemigroupPreimage(S), QuotientSemigroupCongruence(S), and QuotientSemigroupHomomorphism(S) provide access to preimage, congruence, and homomorphism for a quotient semigroup S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotient semigroups have elements that are congruence classes; the manual advises using Elements or the quotient homomorphism to examine equivalence classes. For heavy computations consider alternative representations because equality tests may enumerate congruence classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green's relations (R, L, J, H, D) and their semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Green's relations R, L, J, H, D are equivalence relations on a semigroup: x R y iff xS^1 = yS^1; x L y iff S^1x = S^1y; x J y iff S^1 x S^1 = S^1 y S^1; H = R ∧ L; D = R ◦ L. R, L, J induce preorders and partial orders on their equivalence classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These relations are fundamental in semigroup theory and are available in GAP as attributes and functions; the documentation describes their algebraic meaning and ordering relations among classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: GreensRRelation / GreensLRelation / GreensJRelation / GreensDRelation / GreensHRelation
rubrics_metrics.description: GreensRRelation(semigroup) etc. return the corresponding Green's relation (as attributes) for the semigroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes allow programmatic access to the relations; several utility functions build on them (e.g., GreensRClasses).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGreensRelation / IsGreensXRelation
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGreensRelation(bin-relation) and the typed versions IsGreensRRelation, IsGreensLRelation, IsGreensJRelation, IsGreensHRelation, IsGreensDRelation check whether a given relation is one of Green's relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to validate relations or classify an equivalence relation computed by other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGreensClass / IsGreensXClass
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGreensClass(equiv-class) and typed versions (IsGreensRClass, etc.) return true if the equivalence class is a Green's class (of the given type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are filters to verify that an equivalence class object represents a Green-class recognized by GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGreensLessThanOrEqual
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGreensLessThanOrEqual(C1, C2) returns true if Green's class C1 is ≤ C2 under the respective Green ordering (defined via containment of generated principal ideals). Only defined for R, L and J classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare Green's classes with respect to their natural preorders/partial orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: RClassOfHClass / LClassOfHClass
rubrics_metrics.description: RClassOfHClass(H) and LClassOfHClass(H) return the R-class and L-class respectively that contain the H-class H. They reflect the natural ordering over the Green classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for navigating from an H-class to its containing R or L class.

rubrics_metrics.name: EggBoxOfDClass
rubrics_metrics.description: EggBoxOfDClass(Dclass) returns a matrix for a Green's D-class whose rows represent R-classes and columns represent L-classes; entries are the H-classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the 'egg-box' decomposition of a D-class; DisplayEggBoxOfDClass displays a matrix-like picture with 1s and 0s where 1 denotes a group H-class. Useful for visualizing D-class structure and regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: GreensXClassOfElement and GreensXClasses
rubrics_metrics.description: GreensRClassOfElement(S,a), GreensLClassOfElement(S,a), GreensDClassOfElement(S,a), GreensJClassOfElement(S,a), GreensHClassOfElement(S,a) create the respective Green class of element a in S. GreensRClasses(S) etc. return the list of R-, L-, H-, J-, or D-classes of S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these operations to compute individual classes or all classes of a given type; EquivalenceClasses can be used for Green relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: GroupHClassOfGreensDClass
rubrics_metrics.description: GroupHClassOfGreensDClass(Dclass) returns a group H-class contained in the D-class Dclass, or fail if none exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A D-class may or may not contain group H-classes; this gives access to one if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGroupHClass
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGroupHClass(Hclass) returns true iff the H-class Hclass is a group, which is equivalent to Hclass^2 intersecting Hclass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing if an H-class is a group is an important structural property; the manual gives the algebraic characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRegularDClass
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRegularDClass(Dclass) returns true if every element of the Green D-class Dclass is regular. A D-class is regular iff any one of its elements is regular; regular D-classes contain idempotents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This predicate is helpful in structural decomposition; the manual cites the theorem that idempotents imply regularity (Howie reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: DisplaySemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: DisplaySemigroup(S) produces a convenient display of a transformation semigroup's D-class structure: for each rank r ≤ n (degree), it shows all D-classes of rank r and marks regular D-classes and sizes of H-classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to get a human-readable overview of a transformation semigroup's D-class structure; regular D-classes with a single H-class show as '*[H size = ..., ...]'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rees matrix / Rees 0-matrix semigroup definitions and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A Rees matrix semigroup over S with index sets I and J and matrix P = (p_{j,i}) is I × S × J with multiplication (i,s,j)(k,t,l) = (i, s·p_{j,k}·t, l). A Rees 0-matrix semigroup adjoins a zero and multiplies to 0 when the corresponding matrix entry is 0. Rees matrix semigroups over groups are exactly the completely simple semigroups; Rees 0-matrix semigroups over groups are completely 0-simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important structural construction: subsemigroups of Rees matrix semigroups need not themselves be Rees matrix semigroups. The documentation explains uniqueness of the family/semi-group containing Rees elements and how isomorphisms to Rees forms can be computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReesMatrixSemigroup / ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: ReesMatrixSemigroup(S, mat) returns the Rees matrix semigroup defined by matrix mat over semigroup S. ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(S, mat) returns the Rees 0-matrix semigroup; in GAP a Rees 0-matrix semigroup always contains a multiplicative zero element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show constructing R := ReesMatrixSemigroup(G, mat) and ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(DihedralGroup(...), mat). The returned object is a full Rees matrix semigroup family; elements belong to that family and cannot be multiplied with elements from other families.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReesMatrixSubsemigroup / ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: ReesMatrixSubsemigroup(R, I, U, J) and ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup(R, I, U, J) return the (0-)Rees subsemigroup generated by I × U × J where I ⊆ rows(R), J ⊆ columns(R), and U is a subsemigroup of the underlying semigroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to construct subsemigroups by specifying row/column index subsets and underlying subsemigroup. Examples illustrate constructing subsemigroups and testing IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup / IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup(S) (and the 0-matrix variant) returns an isomorphism from a finite simple semigroup S to a Rees matrix semigroup over a group (or error if S is not simple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every finite simple semigroup is isomorphic to a Rees matrix semigroup over a group; use these functions to compute that isomorphism when applicable. For non-(0-)simple input the function returns an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement / IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement
rubrics_metrics.description: Category predicates IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement(elt) and IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement(elt) return true if elt is an element of a Rees matrix (or 0-matrix) semigroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check element membership-type to ensure operations that assume Rees matrix element structure are safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReesMatrixSemigroupElement / ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement
rubrics_metrics.description: ReesMatrixSemigroupElement(R, i, x, j) and ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement(R, i, x, j) construct the Rees matrix (or 0-matrix) semigroup element with row i, underlying element x, and column j (if such an element exists). The components can be recovered by y[1], y[2], y[3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful constructor/accessor for elements of Rees (0-)matrix semigroups. Example: ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement(R,1,(1,2,3),2) yields (1,(1,2,3),2).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup(R) and IsReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup(R) return true if R is a semigroup consisting of elements of some Rees matrix (0-matrix) semigroup (i.e., every semigroup of such elements satisfies this property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: being a subsemigroup of a Rees matrix semigroup does not imply R itself is a Rees matrix semigroup (see IsReesMatrixSemigroup predicate).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsReesMatrixSemigroup / IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsReesMatrixSemigroup(R) returns true iff a subsemigroup R of I×U×J equals I'×U'×J' for some I'⊆I, J'⊆J and U' a subsemigroup of U. Analogous statement for IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup. It can be costly to check for generator-defined subsemigroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect when a subsemigroup has the full Rees matrix semigroup structure (i.e., product of index sets and underlying semigroup). Examples illustrate cases where the predicate is true or false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix / MatrixOfReesMatrixSemigroup / MatrixOfReesZeroMatrixSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrix(R) (or MatrixOfReesMatrixSemigroup / MatrixOfReesZeroMatrixSemigroup) returns the matrix used to define multiplication in the Rees matrix or 0-matrix semigroup R. If R is a proper subsemigroup of a larger family, Matrix returns the family-defining matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbitrary subsemigroups may not have a matrix; they do only if IsReesMatrixSemigroup or IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup holds. The function returns the construction matrix, which can be larger than the apparent dimensions of R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rows and Columns of Rees matrix semigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Rows(R) and Columns(R) return the row and column index sets of the Rees matrix or 0-matrix semigroup R. Note: rows of the semigroup correspond to columns of the defining matrix and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes exist only if R satisfies IsReesMatrixSemigroup/IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup. Examples show Rows(R) and Columns(R) returning ranges or lists of indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingSemigroup (for Rees matrix semigroup)
rubrics_metrics.description: UnderlyingSemigroup(R) returns the underlying semigroup S used in the Rees matrix or 0-matrix semigroup R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available only if R satisfies the Rees matrix semigroup predicate; used to access the S in I × S × J constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AssociatedReesMatrixSemigroupOfDClass
rubrics_metrics.description: AssociatedReesMatrixSemigroupOfDClass(D) returns a Rees matrix or 0-matrix semigroup associated to a regular D-class D of a finite semigroup S. If D is a subsemigroup it is isomorphic to a Rees matrix semigroup; otherwise one defines a semigroup on D ∪ {0} making it 0-simple and returns the corresponding Rees 0-matrix semigroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constructs the standard Rees (0-)matrix semigroup associated to a D-class; useful for decomposing finite semigroups into Rees components and for explicit isomorphism computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely presented semigroups/monoids (definition and caveats)
rubrics_metrics.description: A finitely presented semigroup (resp. monoid) is a quotient of a free semigroup (resp. free monoid) on finitely many generators by a finitely generated congruence (i.e., a finite set of relations as pairs of words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important computational caveat: equality testing and other computations in finitely presented semigroups can be undecidable in general; algorithms in GAP may run forever, run out of memory, or raise warnings. If the fp semigroup is known to be finite theory-guarantees termination (given enough memory) but runtime is not a priori bounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating fp semigroup/monoid: / (or \/) operator and FactorFree*ByRelations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use F / rels or \/(F, rels) to create the finitely presented semigroup/monoid given by presentation <gens | rels>. FactorFreeSemigroupByRelations and FactorFreeMonoidByRelations also return the fp semigroup/monoid for a free semigroup/monoid F and relations rels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show constructing fs := FreeSemigroup(3) and s := fs / [ [ x1*x2*x1, x1 ], [ x2^4, x1 ] ]. Note: some older functions (FactorFree*) are not called by the infix operator and may be removed in future revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generator names and element identity in fp objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Generator display names are not variables; they are just printed/display figures. To access generators programmatically you must bind them as variables (e.g., a := s.1). Generators of the free object differ from generators of the factored fp object even if displayed with same names, so words in the free semigroup are not elements of the quotient without mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show trying to refer to 'a' before binding yields an error. Use the object's indexing (s.1, s.2, ...) to reference generators of the finitely presented object.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup / IsSubmonoidFpMonoid and IsFpSemigroup / IsFpMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup(t) returns true if t is a finitely presented semigroup or a subsemigroup of a finitely presented semigroup. IsSubmonoidFpMonoid is the monoid analogue. IsFpSemigroup(s) and IsFpMonoid(m) are synonyms for checking whole-family/finitely-presented status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful filters to determine whether semigroup/monoid objects are fp or substructures of fp objects. Typical construction: Semigroup(gens) or Monoid(gens) where gens are elements of an fp object.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsElementOfFpSemigroup / IsElementOfFpMonoid and FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement
rubrics_metrics.description: Category predicate IsElementOfFpSemigroup(elm) returns true if elm is an element of a finitely presented semigroup (analogous for monoid). FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement(elm) returns the finitely presented group/monoid/semigroup to which elm belongs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show checking elements and recovering the parent fp object for given elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismFpSemigroup / IsomorphismFpMonoid / IsomorphismFpMonoid for groups
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismFpSemigroup(m) (and IsomorphismFpMonoid(g) for groups) returns an isomorphism from the given finitely presented monoid or group to a finitely presented semigroup or monoid representation (e.g., expanding group generators to include inverses in monoid representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show MappingByFunction objects returned that map elements between the representations; useful for converting between fp group/monoid/semigroup presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality test in finitely presented semigroups (\=)
rubrics_metrics.description: \=(a,b) tests equality of two elements a and b in a finitely presented semigroup. Though equality is defined algebraically, the computation may take a very long time or not terminate due to undecidability issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with caution: fundamental decision problems mean that such tests cannot be guaranteed to finish in the general case. The manual references section 52.5 for further discussion (not included in this chunk).
